name: Russian Bank
description: Russian Bank is a competitive patience game for two players, played with two standard 52-card packs (one per player). Each player has a reserve, hand, and waste pile; they build eight shared foundations (Ace to King by suit) and an eight-column tableau in descending alternating colors, and may load cards onto the opponent's reserve or waste. First to play off all cards wins; opponents may call Stop on an illegal or omitted compulsory move.

Country/Region of Origin: Europe
Time Period: Early 1900s
Historical Development: The game evolved from traditional card games in the region
Cultural Significance: Popular social and family game

Minimum Players: 2
Maximum Players: 2
Optimal Players: 2
Partnerships: None

Type: Standard 52-card deck
Number of Decks: 2 (one per player)
Jokers: Not included

Two standard 52-card packs (different backs recommended)
Score sheet (optional)
Table space

Each player shuffles the other's pack. Each deals from own pack: 12 face-down + 1 face-up (reserve), 4 face-up in a column above reserve (houses). Thirty-five cards remain as hand. Space between tableau columns for eight foundation piles.

items.text: Waste pile available: Top card of your own waste pile is available like tableau outermost cards; must be played to foundation when possible, or to tableau or opponent's reserve/waste when it fits.
Reserve 11 or 12 cards: Some play with an initial reserve of 11 or 12 cards rather than 13; hands are then correspondingly larger.
